title: British Museum presents major exhibition of early Netherlandish drawings
summary: A new exhibition from the British Museum explores the transformative time when Netherlandish drawings emerged from the workshop to become an art form in their own right. Early Netherlandish drawings brings together 110 works by renowned artists such as Rogier van der Weyden, Lucas van Leyden, Pieter Bruegel the elder and Hendrick Goltzius. Lesser-known masters, anonymous sheets and workshop copies have been included to offer a rich and comprehensive account of drawing across the region. The British Museum's collection of pre-1600s Netherlandish drawings, totalling more than 1,200, is one of the most important in the world. Unlike Italy, where the taste for collecting drawings in the 1500s ensured that a higher number from previous centuries were preserved, early Netherlandish works on paper are much rarer. The unparalleled breadth and quality of the Museum's holdings in this field provide an opportunity to piece together this sometimes-fragmented narrative.

title: Kunst der Westküste explores the early impulses of northern modernism
summary: This exhibition is devoted to a fascinating chapter in the history of European art: the early impulses of modern art in the north. From the Netherlands to Norway, new perspectives on light, colour and nature emerged along the coast – far from urban centres but always in a vibrant dialogue with them. Here “modernism” means more than just artistic styles , it is an attitude: the courage to call into question what can be seen , to shift perspectives and to set a new way of thought in motion. Sustained by individuals or worked out in artists’ colonies – the spark of modernism was gradually ignited along the edge of the continent. Based on the museum's own collection and enriched by important international loans, the exhibition highlights places where modernism encountered the sea – and tells the stories behind the pictures. title: Adrián Villar Rojas challenges human exceptionalism in major Aspen Art Museum exhibition
summary: Running from July 2 to April 11, 2027, across two floors of the Museum, Adrián Villar Rojas: First Gods, Lost Animals evokes both the geological and mythological formation of a cave. In Villar Rojas’s approach, the cave functions as a space of double accumulation: geologically shaped through eons of material deposition and mineral consolidation, and culturally layered with human projections, rituals, and symbolic activity. The exhibition is grounded in the premise that humans, as finite intelligences, confront a universe whose complexity far exceeds their cognitive scale. In this condition, symbolic tools arise—gods, art, mathematics—as adaptive technologies that render the world navigable. title: Baltimore Museum of Art announces major acquisitions with 118 artworks entering the collection
summary: The Baltimore Museum of Art announced today that it has acquired approximately 118 works over the past six months, deepening its holdings of both historical and contemporary objects from across the globe as well as by talented artists throughout the Baltimore region. This includes a gift of 64 works from Constance R. Caplan, a former BMA board chair who has been actively engaged with the museum since 1955, and whose collection was the subject of an exhibition at the Art Institute of Chicago in 2020. The gift includes important works by Janine Antoni, Hilla and Bernd Becher, John Chiara, Fernanda Gomes, Robert Morris, Stephen Parrino, Nobuo Sekine, Richard Tuttle, Lee Ufan, Jack Whitten, Lisa Yuskavage, and others. Among the other acquisitions, which include works entering the collection through purchase and gift or promised gift, are paintings by Katharine Gilbert Riggs Elmore, Inoue Hakuyō, Titus Kaphar, K.S. title: New OKCMOA installation explores Pop, Minimalist, and postwar art movements
summary: The Oklahoma City Museum of Art announces From Pop to Minimalist Art, a single-gallery installation on the Museum’s third floor. Highlights include two loans from Art Bridges Foundation: Andy Warhol’s Coca-Cola [3] from 1962 and Keith Haring’s Self Portrait from 1985. Warhol and Haring’s works are examples of the Pop Art tradition of using text, mechanical reproduction, and commercial symbols to transform images from advertising, popular culture, and everyday life. Coca-Cola [3] marked the beginning of Warhol's signature Pop Art style and is among his earliest depictions of the Coca-Cola bottle, an image that would become a recurring subject throughout his career. Haring’s Self Portrait showcases the artist’s familiar graphic linework while presenting a rare self-portrait. Other movements featured in the installation include Op Art, the Washington Color School, Hard-Edge painting, and Minimalism, along with works by contemporary artists

title: Midlands Arts Centre presents kinetic auction exhibition by Michael Pinsky
summary: Midlands Arts Centre presents The Final Bid: a unique exhibition by internationally renowned artist Michael Pinsky which challenges our desire to buy new things. Transforming the gallery into a powerful immersive installation, Pinsky uses one universal everyday object — the chair — to explore the environmental impact of manufactured goods and encourage audiences to rethink the value of reuse, ownership and the circular economy. At the heart of the exhibition is a live online auction featuring chairs generously donated by members of the public. Suspended dramatically from the ceiling, the 72 selected chairs respond in real time to the value of incoming bids, rising and shifting to create a dynamic kinetic sculpture that visualises demand, desire and consumption. Audiences can submit bids for their favourite chairs by visiting the gallery in person or viewing MAC’s auction platform online. title: Reading Public Museum acquires rare painting by Adam Mortimer Lightner
summary: The Foundation for the Reading Public Museum announced the acquisition of Cupid Riding a Dolphin (1838), a rare painting by Pennsylvania artist Adam Mortimer Lightner (1815–1840). The acquisition strengthens the Museum's holdings of early American art while bringing renewed attention to the remarkable achievements of a gifted regional painter whose promising career was cut tragically short. Born into a prominent Lancaster County family, Lightner received his earliest artistic training with John Beck of Lititz before continuing his studies in Philadelphia through the Artists' Fund Society, established in 1835. Among the influential Pennsylvania artists who encouraged his early development were Jacob Eichholtz (1776–1842), Bass Otis (1784–1861), and Joshua Shaw (1776–1861). title: Early Maya calendrical writing identified in Pre-Hispanic mural at Calakmul
summary: A newly reconstructed mural from the ancient Maya city of Calakmul has revealed what researchers believe is an early example of calendrical writing, adding the site to a select group of major Maya centers associated with the development of writing and monumental culture during the Late Preclassic period. The mural, discovered inside Structure II at the archaeological site, depicts the mythical hero Juun Ajaw hunting a creature in the water. Alongside the scene, researchers identified a sign corresponding to a day marker from the Maya 260-day ritual calendar. The finding is particularly significant because most of the surviving inscriptions at Calakmul date from the Classic period, between AD 250 and 900. Until now, archaeologists had found no clear evidence of written communication at the city from the much earlier Preclassic era. title: New exhibition explores cross-cultural dialogues in Australian art
summary: TarraWarra Museum of Art opened its group exhibition, Inside the Mirage, shaped by the imaginative and philosophical worlds of artists Ian Fairweather (1891–1974) and John Young (b. 1956), curated by TarraWarra Museum of Art Curator James Lynch. Drawing these two practices into dialogue, the exhibition, on view at the Museum from 25 July until 1 November 2026, highlights new perspectives and connections between Australian art history and the present. Alongside Young and Fairweather, the exhibition features nine contemporary artists from across Australia whose works foreground shared and inherited stories as their basis, revealing the intertwined histories and complex cultural narratives that shape our contemporary identities and worldviews. title: International Puppet Fringe Festival unveils landmark exhibition offerings
summary: This August, the newly renovated Clemente Soto Vélez Cultural & Educational Center will become one of the country's most dynamic destinations for contemporary puppetry and visual theater as it hosts an expansive exhibition program presented as part of the 4th International Puppet Fringe Festival (IPFF). Spanning multiple galleries, public spaces, and installations throughout the historic Lower East Side cultural center, the exhibitions invite visitors to experience puppetry as sculpture, installation, photography, cultural artifact, and contemporary art. The exhibitions open August 12. title: Latvian National Museum of Art presents contemporary drawings from Centre Pompidou
summary: From 25 July to 1 November 2026, the left wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga hosts the exhibition Contemporary Drawings: Florence and Daniel Guerlain’s Donation and Gifts to Centre Pompidou. This exhibition is an internationally significant and artistically highly valuable collaboration project between the Latvian National Museum of Art (LNMA) and Centre Pompidou. It presents works from the collection donated by collectors and art patrons Florence and Daniel Guerlain to the French institution over the past twenty years. The Guerlain collection is thematically diverse and distinctly contemporary in nature. From the donation of nearly 1200 works, a multifaceted selection for the exhibition in Riga has been curated, featuring 98 drawings by 43 artists of different nationalities

title: Ashley Saville presents group exhibition examining beauty, desire, and abjection
summary: Ashley Saville presents La Belle et la Bête, the first group exhibition at 193 Fleet Street. The exhibition takes its title from Gabrielle-Suzanne Barbot de Villeneuve’s fairytale of the same name, a text that has bewitched artists, musicians, and filmmakers since its anonymous publication in 1740. A young woman is trapped in an enchanted castle with a beastly creature. At first she loathes him, but eventually her heart softens. Her declaration of true love breaks the Beast’s curse: he transforms into a handsome prince, and they live happily ever after. Though rooted in a moralising literary tradition, La Belle et la Bête resists simple binaries of good and evil. Desire and abjection, duty and transgression, ideals and outsiders are not fundamental oppositions; rather, they are intricately imbricated aspects of life and love. title: Guggenheim unveils major exhibition tracing the legacy of Pop art
summary: The Guggenheim New York unveiled Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now, a focused exhibition exploring the museum’s holdings of Pop art and the movement’s enduring influence on artists working around the world today. Drawing on the institution’s history, Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now illuminates a lesser-known chapter in the museum’s past while foregrounding the significant contributions of both historical and contemporary practices. Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now features an eclectic selection of major works from the collection by 29 artists, including John Chamberlain, Chryssa, Jim Dine, Richard Hamilton, Yayoi Kusama, Roy Lichtenstein, Marta Minujín, Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen, Lucas Samaras,

title: Artist Catalina Africa explores inner landscapes in new series of paintings at Silverlens
summary: mirrors, merging is Catalina Africa’s new body of paintings that step into the innerscape of transitions. The world is seen and called anew, as Catalina precipitates otherworldly territories into works that test flow forms, dissolution, and the slow collapse of inner terrain into the landscape it mirrors. Five paintings in mirrors, merging are the steles that surround this mystery, registering a painter’s devotional process at thresholds of life and practice. Catalina’s process across her five paintings moves like a single gesture stretched out over time, in which space is claimed, the ground is prepared, tributes are gathered, energy rises, and finally, there is release. Mirrors, Merging is a terrain of intention, where the cross-section of gestation lines the edges of emanation. title: Rare Mexico City 1968 Olympic 'Type 6' torch sells for $91,451 at auction
summary: A rare Mexico City 1968 Summer Olympics ‘Type 6’ torch, accompanied by its original Spanish torch relay participation medal, sold for $91,451 to lead RR Auction’s Olympics sale, which closed July 23. The Type 6 torch is one of the rarest documented variations produced for the 1968 Olympic torch relay. Developed after an explosion during a flame-transfer ceremony in Barcelona prompted safety concerns among organizers, the simplified design was introduced for use during portions of the relay in Spain. The existence of the Type 6 torch remained largely unknown until nearly 50 years after the Games, when Olympic researchers authenticated the model through contemporary photographs and archival documentation. title: Artist Joiri Minaya challenges colonial myths of the Tropics in new Seattle show
summary: Joiri Minaya (b.1990, New York City; raised in the Dominican Republic) is a multidisciplinary artist who examines the Tropics as a constructed place and identity. As both performer and saboteur, Minaya challenges misrepresentations that reduce tropical geographies and their inhabitants to imagined fantasies of the colonial imagination. In her work, she reclaims Afro-Indigenous narratives of resistance, ancestral knowledges, and regenerative practices—especially those rooted in plant and botanical traditions. The exhibition at the Henry will showcase the versatile language of textiles that Minaya has developed to critique the making of a global Tropics—a fabricated realm for the “exotic” extending from the Caribbean to the Pacific. title: Contemporary Now returns to Chennai for expanded third edition
summary: Conceived as a platform for dialogue, discovery and exchange, Contemporary Now brings together India's leading galleries in a shared presentation of contemporary art. What began as a collaborative curatorial initiative has evolved into one of the country's most exciting recurring art platforms, fostering meaningful connections between artists, galleries, and audiences. The third edition of Contemporary Now, taking place from 8–25 August 2026, is its most ambitious yet, transforming Chennai into a vibrant destination for contemporary art through an expansive programme. The exhibition will take place across two floors of Lalit Kala Akademi, with partner programmes unfolding across venues throughout Chennai. title: Incisive class satire executiveproduced by Jia Zhangke opens Aug. 28 at Film Forum
summary: Film Forum will present the U.S. theatrical premiere of Rafael Manuel’s Filipiñana on Friday, August 28. 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, Filipiñana unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence. title: Photoszene Köln to explore uncertainty and the limits of photographic knowledge
summary: What can photography reveal—and what remains beyond its reach? This question will guide Not Knowing — Photography and the Unknown, a four-day congress presented by the Internationale Photoszene Köln from October 22 to 25, 2026, at the Orangerie Theater in Cologne. Bringing together artists, scholars, archivists, designers, performers and thinkers from a wide range of disciplines, the congress will examine photography not simply as a tool for documenting reality or producing knowledge, but as a medium shaped by uncertainty, absence, projection and speculation. The event will serve as the discursive opening of the 2027 Photoszene Festival and will focus on what becomes possible when not knowing is treated not as a weakness, but as a productive condition. title: Festival d'Aix-en-Provence closes 78th edition with nearly 64,000 spectators
summary: The Festival d’Aix-en-Provence concluded its 78th edition after welcoming nearly 64,000 spectators across a wide-ranging program of opera, concerts, public talks, screenings and educational initiatives. Held from July 2 to 21, 2026, the edition was conceived by Pierre Audi and presented as a tribute to his artistic vision and dedication to the festival. More than 38,000 seats were filled for operas and concerts during the July program, while almost 26,000 people attended the festival’s free events. These included the Aix en juin pre-festival program, performances by the Orchestre des Jeunes de la Méditerranée, film screenings, public rehearsals, talks and introductory events. title: Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art presents major solo show by Chitra Ganesh
summary: Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art is presenting the first major solo exhibition in a UK institution by artist Chitra Ganesh. Journey to the Great Below features a new animation, newly commissioned sculptural works and a site-specific wall drawing, alongside a selection of recent paintings, prints, works on paper and mixed media works. Ganesh’s practice is rooted in drawing and painting and has a distinctive multidisciplinary approach. Over the past twenty-five years, she has developed an expansive body of work that encompasses wall drawings, collage, animation, installation, and sculpture. title: Nasher Museum of Art announces fall exhibitions
summary: The Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University announced its fall 2026 exhibition season, featuring major presentations that examine the enduring power of art to reflect, challenge, and shape society. Spanning early American history to contemporary global perspectives, the season explores democracy, citizenship, protest, and identity through exhibitions that invite visitors to consider who is represented in the nation’s founding ideals and how individuals and communities continue to advocate for change. title: Whitney Museum and the Pinault Collection join OFFSCREEN's "Acquisitions and Discoveries" programme
summary: This fall, OFFSCREEN Paris returns to the Chapelle Saint-Louis de la Salpêtrière from October 20 to 25,2026 (VIP preview October 19). For its fifth edition, the event honors Ana Mendieta and welcomes Pinault Collection and the Whitney Museum of American Art in its Acquisitions and Discoveries program. OFFSCREEN Paris is a nomadic event that values contemporary, historic and avant-garde artists with experimental image-based practices. With its distinct voice, it is a must-see highlight of Paris Art Week each October, bringing together a tightly curated selection of artists working with installations, still and moving images. For the second year in a row, OFFSCREEN invites two major cultural institutions to take part in its Acquisitions and Discoveries program.
